newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal sees 400 bln esc from 1997 privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Portugal sees 400 bln esc from 1997 privatisations.

text.p: The Portuguese state should generate at least 400 billion escudos from privatisions next year, according to a government outline of the 1997 budget.
The budget outline forecast the ratio of public debt to gross domestic product (GDP) would fall to 68 percent next year from between 69 and 70 percent at present, boosted by privatisation revenue.
Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said in New York earlier this month that the state could raise 450 billion escudos from privatisations in 1996, well above its target of 380 billion.

Following the sale of a second tranche of Portugal Telecom this summer, the government is due to sell off stakes in tobacco producer Tabaqueira, cement firm Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal SA and Banco Totta e Acores by the end of the year.
Next year the state plans to sell off further stakes in Telecom, pulp concern Portucel Industrial and oil firm Petrogal.

The outline reiterated earlier government forecasts for Portugal's budget deficit. It said the deficit would fall to 2.9 percent of GDP next year and would probably be below the 4.2 percent originally forecast for 1996.
"If exchange rates remain steady and barring economic calamities abroad the inflation rate should remain below 2.5 percent," the outline said.
